_comment: SYNTHETIC — hand-built from the documented response shapes in Yahoo's official
Fantasy Sports API guide and from published wrapper-library samples (yfpy,
yahoo_fantasy_api). NOT a live capture. Yahoo API access is gated behind an
approval application and NO live call has ever been made from this repo.
Replace with a real redacted capture once API access is approved.
AUTHORED 2026-08-11 (not captured on any date).
MODELS: GET /fantasy/v2/league/461.l.576919/transactions?format=json
(one 3-player, 2-team trade extracted from that collection)
REDACTION: all identifiers invented — team keys, team names, transaction ids
and the trade note are fake. Player names are real NFL players with PLAUSIBLE
BUT UNVERIFIED numeric ids. No token, email, real GUID or real league key
appears anywhere in this directory.
⚠️ THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT FIXTURE IN THE SET. It is the LIST-OF-ONE-DICT
half of the transaction_data shape trap:
add/drop:  "transaction_data": { ... }      ← a bare object
TRADE:     "transaction_data": [ { ... } ]  ← a list containing ONE object
Yahoo uses the list form for trades because a traded asset can in principle
carry several movement records. Nothing announces the difference. Code that
assumes the bare-dict form reads a trade leg as a list, finds no 'type' key,
and produces a transaction with ZERO assets — or skips it entirely. The
result is a transaction log with every waiver move present and every trade
missing, which looks exactly like a league that does not trade. No exception
is raised at any point. parse_transactions() sends both shapes through
as_list(); this file is the only thing that proves the list branch works.
WHAT THE TRADE IS: 3 player legs across 2 teams. t.4 sends TWO players to
t.11 and receives ONE back. Correct parsing yields exactly 3 rows in
fantasy_transaction_assets, all sharing transaction_key
'461.l.576919.tr.163', with leg_index 0,1,2 and asset_count 3 on the parent.
A parser that mishandles the list shape yields 0 — the failure is total, not
partial, which is why the count is the assertion worth writing.
OTHER SHAPE HAZARDS DELIBERATELY PRESENT:
1. Every leg has BOTH a source_team_key and a destination_team_key. In a
trade neither side is a pool, so unlike a waiver claim nothing is
absent — the mirror image of yahoo_transaction_faab_waiver.json.
2. The transaction carries trader_team_key / trader_team_name /
tradee_team_key / tradee_team_name. These are REAL Yahoo fields that
parse_transactions() does not consume, so they must show up in the row's
unmapped_fields list rather than vanishing. That is the mechanism by
which a provider field we have not modelled becomes visible instead of
silently dropped — assert on it.
3. Player metadata is a LIST NESTED INSIDE the player resource array, one
single-key dict per field.
4. "Ja'Marr Chase" carries a typographic apostrophe in the display name and
a plain one in the ascii fields — normalize_name() must reduce both to
'jamarr chase'. Name normalization is FALLBACK MATCHING ONLY and never
sufficient on its own; it is here to be exercised, not trusted.
5. status is 'successful'. REJECTED and VETOED trades are NOT RETRIEVABLE
from Yahoo at all — they cannot appear in any fixture because they do
not exist in the API. That is a permanent gap, recorded as not_exposed.
NOT EXERCISED HERE: draft-pick legs (transaction['picks']). Yahoo supports
trading picks and parse_transactions() emits asset_kind='draft_pick' rows for
them, but this league does not trade picks and inventing that structure
without a reference capture would be guessing at a shape rather than
recording one.
NOT TRUNCATED: one complete transaction, isolated from the surrounding
collection so a failure here is unambiguous.

transaction.trade_note: Depth for a WR1. Good luck the rest of the way.
